After weeks of ChatGPT users being limited only by weekly usage caps, OpenAI announced today that it will restore the 5-hour usage limit for Codex and ChatGPT Work for Plus subscribers. Details below.

5-hour cap returns for ChatGPT Plus subscribers

Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux, head of Codex and ChatGPT engineering at OpenAI, announced tonight that starting tomorrow (the 25th), the 5-hour usage limit for Codex and ChatGPT Work will be restored for Plus subscribers.

After users hit the 5-hour or weekly usage cap, they can choose to wait for the next cycle to reset their usage, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI will also occasionally reset user limits for free, and stored reset counts can be obtained through designated promotions and referral offers.

However, over the past few weeks, OpenAI temporarily removed the 5-hour usage limit for Codex and ChatGPT Work, keeping only the weekly cap.

During this period, the company also reset users' weekly usage multiple times ahead of schedule, to celebrate milestones, including reaching an additional one million active users across the two (now unified) platforms.

However, Tibo explained tonight on X:

"Tomorrow we will restore the 5-hour cap for Plus accounts on ChatGPT Work and Codex. I mentioned this earlier but then postponed it. This is necessary because (a) the 5-hour cap allows us to allocate computing resources more smoothly, thereby keeping the plan generous in terms of weekly usage; (b) most Plus plan users are relatively casual new users, but they will also inadvertently exhaust their usage for the entire week, then feel confused, resulting in a not-so-great experience. Over the coming months, we will keep the 5-hour cap disabled for Pro $100 and Pro $200 subscriptions."

Tibo did not mention any changes to Enterprise or Edu accounts, which currently use a separate credit-based usage system.

Will the restoration of the 5-hour cap for ChatGPT Work and Codex affect you? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
